item.title: U. Arizona professor alleges retaliation for opposing DEI hiring practices
item.description: A tenured University of Arizona professor recently filed a lawsuit against the school, alleging retaliation for opposing what he believed were race-based hiring practices tied to “diversity, equity, and inclusion” initiatives. Professor Matthew Abraham claims the university sanctioned and excluded him from key faculty committees after he raised concerns about DEI hiring policies and sought […]

item.title: Ignore, but laugh at, dopey leftists who ruin Christmas (and other) entertainment
item.description: Progressives relentlessly attempt to impose their views on entertainment, arguing that classics like "Planes, Trains and Automobiles" and "It's a Wonderful Life" promote harmful messages. This ideological editing has disappointed fans of various franchises. However, there are signs of a cultural shift as audiences seek original, unaltered content and traditional networks gain popularity.

item.title: Instructor who showed Trump inauguration video ‘likened to a terrorist’
item.description: A British teacher faced referral to the counter-terrorism program for showing Trump inauguration videos in class, leading to allegations of emotional harm and potential hate crime. After an investigation into perceived bias, he was warned and settled for £2,000, claiming the actions were politically motivated and detrimental to his mental health.

item.title: Latest on Brown shooting: Custodian warned about shooter, police chief put on leave
item.description: The motive for the attack remains unclear, as the suspected gunman killed himself.

item.title: UC Berkeley community upset at suspension of hunger-struck pro-Palestinian lecturer
item.description: UC Berkeley's pro-Palestinian lecturer, Peyrin Kao, has been suspended without pay, leading to backlash from faculty and students. Critics argue the discipline undermines free speech, noting Kao’s popularity among students and the political nature of the decision. Supporters are demanding clearer guidelines on faculty conduct and have petitioned against the suspension.
